shots.text: Four soldiers picked up a tank and carried it across a field.
Two French cyclists watched, completely stunned.
You see, this tank weighed just ninety-three pounds. It was made of rubber.
In nineteen forty-four, America built a secret unit of about eleven hundred men.
Many were painters, designers, and actors.
Their job was to make eleven hundred men look like a whole army division.
They blew up rubber tanks at night. They painted fake markings on their trucks.
Huge speakers played recordings of tanks rolling, heard miles away.
And fake radio messages filled the air.
But one close look, and the whole trick would be over.
You see, a spy plane sees shapes and shadows, not weight. Like a cardboard cutout in a shop window, it looks real from across the street.
So in March nineteen forty-five, they set up a fake army by the Rhine River. German troops moved to face it, while the real army crossed miles away.
The Army kept it secret for over fifty years, in case they needed the trick again.
